description: redundancy.v1 §2.15, §5: a tool's reading of one address and governed interface -> §5's questions. reading.governance is "claim" or "external" (governed, by contracts read and agreeing), "not_governed", "no_contract" (a candidate's contract not read) or "disagree" (the candidates' revisions disagree on governance or the election); reading.across_face is true across a constrained face (false when absent); reading.first and reading.second are two reads a grace apart, each as elections.json writes one. The holders of a read are its instances with token true; a candidate one whose descriptor is "standby" or "serving". expect.one_incumbent, expect.vacancy and expect.standbys answer of the address, expect.twins of each instance named in either read, by id; each is {answer, reason}, answer one of yes, no, unobservable, not_asked, not_this_profiles, and standbys adds count and exact. The premises, in order, for every question: across_face -> unobservable, across_face; the second read without any instance (for twins, without that instance) -> not_asked, absent when it is complete, else unobservable, presence_incomplete; governance not_governed -> not_this_profiles, not_governed; no_contract -> unobservable, no_contract; disagree -> unobservable, revisions_disagree. Then each question's steps are v1.md §2.15's, in its order: one_incumbent (split, in_transition, one, presence_incomplete, no_descriptor, no_candidate, vacant), vacancy (held, presence_incomplete, no_descriptor, no_candidate, lasting, vacant), standbys (standing_by with the count of the second read's instances marked standby and holding no token, exact when that read is complete and every descriptor in it read; presence_incomplete; no_descriptor; none, count 0, exact), twins (split, split_lowest, no_descriptor, not_a_candidate, unlisted, in_transition, marked_holding, incumbent, presence_incomplete, standby, unmarked). On a premise's answer, standbys has count 0 and exact false.
